scope: Modern C responsibility replacement, historical patches are evidence only. Source and native admission remain separate.

modelDivision.Quint: Temporal handoff histories and explicit negative mutations
modelDivision.Lean: Existing spatial/frame and algebraic obligations only; no duplicate schedule proof
modelDivision.ASCENT: Exact source/profile/evidence closure; LLM is the review environment, not proof

adapters.contract: Reservation is not ownership. The load observing the granted ticket acquires prior owner stores; unlock releases. Try/debug/normal families use the same ordered-word API.
adapters.retired: volatile-only ownership polling and separate global-word aliases
adapters.remaining: Unique origin of historical detached BTQ node not established; diagnostic history records not claimed race-free.

adapters.contract: Private payload write precedes release stamp; every unlocked fast receive acquires the stamp and copies payload before reset. Within a fixed admitted tree the reverse-direction message carries prior consumption before reuse.
adapters.retired: volatile stamps, fence-after-publication premise and reset-before-copy ordering
adapters.remaining: Must refine reverse-message reuse for every membership transition; retained mutex/CV lifetime is separate, not implied by atomic publication.

adapters.contract: Thread lock owns withdrawal through callback; physical owner guards result/release. Durable wait reparks the logical GC-repaired suffix before registering the current Thread.
adapters.retired: Two service bodies, reused mutable request meanings, late continuation authority over a subsequent physical owner
adapters.remaining: Existing bounded lifecycle histories do not prove every physical BTQ writer or actual OS interleaving.

adapters.contract: VM owns acquired-resource bits and retained mutex/CV per processor bound. Exclusive constructor records each successful acquisition, reset does not reconstruct handles, processor cleanup does not destroy them, VM drain disposes only acquired bits.
adapters.retired: None claimed in this candidate for retained-resource lifetime
adapters.remaining: Destructor syscall corruption and arbitrary external/private C entry are not admitted; current priority queue-writer source gap is tracked separately.

adapters.contract: Direct start: Thread initialization/start lease plus destination queue lock. Migration: Thread lease covers saved continuation, destination publication and source withdrawal; never two processor locks held simultaneously. No fixed busy wait.
adapters.remaining: This does not authorize the separate priority reposition writers.

adapters.contract: Known closed/joined VM, or unpublished constructor, owns disposal. A refused POSIX destruction keeps the acquired bit and control; cleanup retry does not repeat completed effects.
adapters.remaining: Unexpected unpublished teardown refusal retains constructor custody; blind retry/free is not licensed.

adapters.contract: Thread lease does not by itself close a queue/key-change transaction; the two raw reposition calls remain unqualified.
adapters.remaining: No-GC/pre-reservation, lock order, key mutation and exception custody require one complete design; no unique-cause attribution from timeout.
